ship_name: Proof was led in Falkirk Sheriff Court on Monday
raw_line: Proof was led in Falkirk Sheriff Court on Monday—before Sheriff-substitute Scott Moncrieff—in the action at the instance of Captain Rasmussen, master of the Norwegian schooner Singborg, against Messrs. J. T. Salvesen and Co., of Grangemouth, for £14 10s. 6d., being balance of freight for a cargo of pit props from Finland, to Grangemouth. It was proved that the schooner Marie arrived at the entrance to Grangemouth Docks on the forenoon of 18th September, but in consequence of a block at the docks was not admitted until 24 hours later. In the meantime the captain had gone ashore, and having no information from his owners or agent for the charterers—Messrs. Chr. Salvesen & Co., London—he applied to Messrs. J. T. Salvesen & Co., shipping agents, Grangemouth, to have the ship reported at the Custom House, which was done by Messrs. Salvesen & Co. It was proved that the ship on her arrival was within the limits of Grangemouth harbour mouth, and that consequently she was entitled to be entered at the Custom House within 24 hours after her arrival. Messrs. Chr. Salvesen & Co.'s shipbroking clerk stated that he did not understand that the ship was to be reported until he received instructions. Evidence was also given to the effect that the fee for clearing a ship of the Singborg's size was about 10s. or one guinea, and that it was also the custom that the agent who reported the vessel got any further business which might arise out of the chartering of the vessel. For the defence, Mr. J. B. Allan, solicitor, contended that the charges had been incurred, in respect that the pursuer failed to intimate his name to the defenders, and that in this case the name of the broker was not mentioned.

There is a deficiency of £466. The debtor alleges his causes of failure to be "illness, slackness of business, depreciation in value of property, and the action brought against me by the executrix of W. Knott to recover £200 on a cheque for which I received no consideration." The Official Receiver's observations were:—The receiving order was made on the petition of a creditor filed 14th May last. The debtor commenced business at a builder at Ryde about forty years ago, and continued to trade there until two years since, when his son purchased from him the stock and book debts. The only asset returned by the debtor in his statement of affairs is the equity of redemption of Havelock Lodge, in which the debtor and his son reside, and which the debtor estimates to be worth £39. The furniture and effects in Havelock Lodge are claimed by the debtor's son and another relative. At the date of the receiving order several judgments had been obtained against the debtor. In 1879 the debtor made a private arrangement with his creditors, paying them 5s. in the pound, and in 1882 he filed a petition for liquidation, under which a dividend of 3s. 6d. in the pound was paid, the debtor not obtaining the discharge. The debtor has not kept a cash book, nor filed a proper account of his insolvency, but attributes his insolvency principally to depreciation in value of properties of which he had been possessed, and which at different times he had sold.

raw_line: Worsbro' Dale- A TIMBER FLUME, fifty-two miles long, has recently been constructed in Fresno Co., Cal., for carrying timber from the Sierra Nevada Mountains to the plain below. The flume is V-shaped on an angle of 90 deg., 3 ft. 7 in. across the top, and 21 in. deep vertically. At minus these dimensions increase to 3 ft. 7 in. and 31 in. In the sides are built of 1 1/2 in. boards, and the flume is carried on trestle-work in some places 130 ft. high. The steepest grade is 1,200 ft. in 5,280 ft., or one mile, for about 3,000 ft., the total fall in that length being 730 ft. The King's River is crossed by a suspension bridge with a stiffening truss, put in by the engineer, Mr. J. M. Graham, to provide for the series of violent undulations which result from the use of the flume. About 9,000,000 ft. B.M. of lumber was used in the construction.

The 20th instant is fixed for the public examination of the debtors.
